problems.statement: The group-wide kitchen is inefficient and slow ticket times (19 vs 12 min) are a problem requiring standardization on par-cooked/frozen components (the client's framing).

The 17-18 minute ticket time at eight locations is a deliberate, board-approved tradeoff of the 'Made Here' made-to-order redesign (pre-forecast 4-5 min increase), which has paid off in satisfaction, food quality, repeat visits, same-store sales, check size and margin.
The 12-minute benchmark is not comparable because the panel only includes chains with at least 60% pre-prepared/frozen components and excludes scratch kitchens, with lower average checks.
Speed of service is the lowest-rated attribute but unchanged since before the redesign (4.2 to 4.1) and does not drive overall satisfaction; server anecdote is not evidence of deterioration.
The group average of 19.1 minutes is inflated by a Riverside-specific deterioration; ex-Riverside it is 17.6, unchanged.

Riverside's real, recent deterioration (27-31 min, ratings and comps worsening) is caused by a staffing gap on the saute/pasta station after the line cook left in August, left unfilled with transfer requests deferred by group operations (the new owners' staffing review).
Riverside's problem is poor leadership by GM Tom Kessler.
Cutting Sunday line hours in June to match covers (down 21% after bridge closure) caused the cook's resignation.
Par-cooked/frozen components would harm the food-quality positioning that drives satisfaction and repeat business, as shown by the 2024 trial.
A 12-minute ticket-time bonus for GMs would invite gaming (KDS bumping) without improving guest experience, as in the 2023 audit.
The repeat-visit rise since Oct 2024 is caused by the menu redesign.

causalClaims.to: ticket time rise of about 4 minutes at all nine locations
higher food quality scores, check size, same-store sales and margin

causalClaims.from: Saute/pasta line cook departure with no replacement or transfer
causalClaims.to: Riverside ticket time spike and falling ratings/comps

causalClaims.from: Group operations deferral of transfers pending staffing review
GM Sunday hour cuts in June
Group ticket time (17-19 min) at other locations

causalClaims.to: what will happen to the rest of the group
gamed reported ticket times without guest benefit
faster ticket times but lower food quality

actions.action: Fill Riverside's saute/pasta vacancy now: approve a transfer cook from another location or expedite hiring, and cross-train/support Jamal; lift the deferral on the GM's transfer requests.
actions.rationale: The KDS, HR and review data localize the entire deterioration to a station gap that group operations itself is holding open.

actions.action: Reject the group-wide move to par-cooked/frozen components.
actions.rationale: The slowness is a board-accepted tradeoff; the benchmark is non-comparable and the 2024 trial showed quality loss, which would erode the positioning behind the check, sales and satisfaction gains.

actions.action: Write a 12-minute ticket-time target into every GM's bonus from Q1 2027.
actions.rationale: Unachievable under the menu, and the 2023 audit showed ticket-time incentives lead to KDS bumping with no guest benefit.

actions.action: Replace Riverside GM Tom Kessler for the ticket-time decline.
actions.rationale: The cause is a staffing gap and deferred requests by group operations; the Sunday-cut link is unconfirmed and the GM acted within the labor standard.

actions.action: Re-baseline the performance review against a comparable scratch-kitchen peer set and track ex-Riverside ticket time against the 19-minute ceiling, plus Riverside recovery after staffing.
actions.rationale: Replaces a misleading benchmark and monitors the accepted ceiling, cheaply and reversibly.

actions.action: Review the group labor-hour standard's effect on Riverside and conduct a proper exit review of why the cook left.
actions.rationale: Conflicting accounts of the departure leave a possible scheduling-policy contribution unresolved.

actions.action: Seek a modest ticket-time reduction at other sites through workflow or station changes that do not alter recipes.
actions.rationale: Only worthwhile if survey data show speed matters to guests at the margin, which current evidence does not show.

nextEvidence: Riverside weekly ticket times and ratings before and after a station staffing fix (natural experiment confirming the causal mechanism)
Ticket times and quality/satisfaction for scratch-kitchen peers or a reconciled repeat-visit measure showing whether speed affects repeat visits
Exit-interview or reasoned account of the cook's departure plus Riverside scheduling policy and Sunday cover history
output.summary: The 'inefficient kitchens' framing is not supported. The 17-18 minute ticket time at eight locations dates to the October 2024 Made Here redesign, a board-accepted tradeoff that coincides with higher food quality, check size, same-store sales, margin and repeat visits. The 12-minute benchmark excludes scratch kitchens. The 19.1 group average is inflated by Riverside, whose collapse traces to an unfilled saute/pasta cook vacancy and transfer requests deferred by group operations. Frozen components would cut quality, and a ticket-time bonus would invite KDS gaming, as in 2023. Fix Riverside staffing; do not replace the GM or standardize the menu.
